- **"No decision" discovery questions:** Why change? / What's the consequence if you don't? / Why now? / Why haven't you done it before, and what's different now? (Ian Koniak — "How to get past 'NO DECISION'")

- Scripts/over-prep reframe: "Scripts were a smoke screen — let go of needing to nail the script; be human, come from abundance, and you get an authentic version back. I'm closing more than ever." (Ian Koniak — "She transformed her sales and life in 6 months!")

- Curiosity-gap words that reliably spark intrigue: "top secret," "unconventional," "lesser known," "unusual approach" (Josh Braun — "What Never to Say in a Meeting Reminder")
- Classic fascination structure to swipe: "What never to eat on an airplane" / the news tease "There's something wrong with your peas — news at 11" (Josh Braun — "What Never to Say in a Meeting Reminder")
- Subject line "The power of Zeus" — pun on the prospect's company name, with a "Zeus" echo on the call (Josh Braun — "Ryan O'Hara Interview")
- One-word follow-up email "Any thoughts?" (no greeting, no name) pulls reply rates equal to the original personalized video (Josh Braun — "How to be a rockstar SDR - Charlotte Johnson")
- LinkedIn profile headline built on top-of-mind pains: "Not booking enough meetings with qualified buyers? Getting ghosted after your first meeting?" (Josh Braun — "Behind the Scenes - How I Leverage LinkedIn to Generate Sales")
- Cold-call opener with a "limiter" to feel exclusive/relevant: "I'm calling small businesses that ship more than 25 packages a month to reduce their shipping cost by 30% — generally speaking, is that interesting?" (Josh Braun — "kevin josh video")
- Problem-led LinkedIn post formula: open with a pain question, white-space each line, end on a CTA ("drop 'interested' in the comments") (Josh Braun — "Behind the Scenes - How I Leverage LinkedIn to Generate Sales")
- "Cold Calling — You're Doing It Wrong" — confrontational "you're doing X wrong" hook frame (Josh Braun — "Cold Calling - You're Doing it Wrong")
- "Why Cold Calling Gives You Anxiety" — name-the-feeling hook that opens by validating a hidden emotional struggle (Josh Braun — "Why Cold Calling Gives You Anxiety")
- Promise the single most important takeaway up front: "If you only have 25 seconds… here's the one thing you need to know… talk less." (Josh Braun — "How to Lead an Initial Save Conversation")
- "It's almost like seeing the code for the Matrix for the first time" — curiosity/transformation hook for reframing how buyers buy (Josh Braun — "How to Nurture Leads")
- Cold-call opener that doubles as a swipeable lead: "I'm just calling to see if you'd be open to a new idea that could help you [specific outcome] — but only if [qualifier]." (Josh Braun — "Cold Calling - You're Doing it Wrong")
- "Can I have 27 seconds to tell you why I'm calling — do you want to meet Tuesday or Wednesday?" shown as the WRONG opener; prospects "can smell your commission breath" (Josh Braun — "Stop 'pitching' in a cold call")
- Curiosity/cliffhanger opener: "We've never met, but I was on your LinkedIn and noticed something interesting about your post — hoping I could ask a couple quick questions" (Josh Braun — "Stop 'pitching' in a cold call")
- Warm-toned cold opener: "Hey [name], we work with a couple other fintech companies in Chicago — it's Armand at Pave. Have you heard our name tossed around?" (Josh Braun — "Sales Messages That Motivates Prospects - Armand Farrokh")
- Pattern-interrupt humor hook: "We're having a competition to see who has the most columns in their merit sheet. The current record is Q-Z, about 452 columns. I think you could win." (Josh Braun — "Sales Messages That Motivates Prospects - Armand Farrokh")
- Humility re-open for burned/dark accounts: "You have absolutely no idea who I am — my name is Josh with DocuSign and I'm just calling to apologize. Do you have a couple minutes?" (Josh Braun — "Clarifying Your Message with Mohammed")
- Self-deprecating permission opener: "My guess is you probably hate cold calls, and frankly I don't love reaching out like this — can I give you the TL;DR of what we do and then you can hang up on me or tell me it's moderately interesting?" (Josh Braun — "Sales Messages That Motivates Prospects - Armand Farrokh")
- LinkedIn headline formula (vs. "Account Executive at Acme"): "We help [WHO] [achieve WHAT]" — e.g. "I help entrepreneurs and VPs of Sales book more meetings with their dream customers" (Josh Braun — "Alison Shutz on How to Land a Job Using LinkedIn")

### Frameworks / formulas
- Objection-handling sequence: **Defuse → Discover → Discuss** — defuse the pressure, find the real underlying reason, then address it (Josh Braun — "Prospect says I don't want a 12-month contract")
- **Problem-train, not product-train** — 5 questions: (1) one specific title you sell to, (2) what job they do daily, (3) how they do it today, (4) the terrible-no-good thing if they keep the status quo, (5) what superpower improves after they pay you (Josh Braun — "How to Nail the First 45 Seconds of a Cold Call")
- Cold-call talk track: Mini-invitation → Scientist discovery ("how are you folks doing X today?") → Poke the bear (question that makes them doubt current solution) → Future-State Cliffhanger (tease the after, go silent) (Josh Braun — "How to Nail the First 45 Seconds of a Cold Call")
- **The Infomercial framework**: paint a specific before-state and after-state; open with "Have you ever…" / "You know how…" (Josh Braun — "Clarifying Raman's Message" / "Overcoming Call Reluctance with Tegan")
- Lead with the PROBLEM, not what you do: "People don't buy your thing — they buy how your thing lets them kick more ass." Open with a relatable problem framed as a question to qualify relevance (Josh Braun — "The 1 Mistake New Reps Make")
- **Open Loop / curiosity-gap mechanic**: create a gap between what they know and what they want to know; "brains crave closure" — tell part of the story, never the whole (Josh Braun — "What Never to Say in a Meeting Reminder")
- **Shine a light** reframe: don't manufacture urgency — surface a risk/problem they didn't know existed and let them create their own doubt; "make something unsafe that they didn't know was unsafe" (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse, We're not interested")
- The "macaroni art" standard: write cold emails good enough you'd be proud to put them on the fridge — personality in the copy exudes confidence (Josh Braun — "Ryan O'Hara Interview")
- Reach-as-currency: the connection request isn't the play — content that earns reach is; treat it like a 401k that compounds over 2-3 years (Josh Braun — "Darren Hull - Building Your Personal Brand")
- Four questions a prospect silently asks, in order (a "no" to any drops you out): 1) Should I pay attention to you? 2) Do I like you? 3) Can you help me do something better? 4) Are you credible? (Josh Braun — "Conversation with Kyle Crawford")
- **"Red X in a sea of white circles"** (David Trott) — the brain ignores patterns, so outreach must pattern-interrupt to earn attention (Josh Braun — "Conversation with Kyle Crawford")
- Sell the deeper benefit, not the feature: people don't buy braces, they buy confidence/a smile (Josh Braun — "Tough Love" / "The One Thing Preventing You From Getting Higher Cold Email Response Rates")
- **"Crispy detail" / metal-detector prospecting**: name the prospect's problem in their exact granular language, ask a question that shines a light on it, then go silent (Josh Braun — "4 Habits That Make Selling More Joyful")
- **Struggle / red-zone framework**: a problem must be big enough to enter the "red zone" before someone switches; nurture everyone else with short, entertaining value content until they self-enter (Josh Braun — "Conversation with Kyle Crawford" / "How to Nurture Leads")
- Cold-call script logic = pre-answer the silent questions in sequence: "Who is this?" → name+company; "Bad time?"; "What do you want?" → one-sentence what-we-do "in a sentence"; close on yes/no "Does that in general sound interesting?" then pivot to "Tell me about your process" regardless (Josh Braun — "kevin josh video")
- **Disqualify-to-sell / the flip**: "If you could double your meetings, could you even handle it?" — framed to disqualify, which makes the prospect sell you on why they're a fit (Josh Braun — "kevin josh video")
- Three-part LinkedIn growth engine: make people smarter, in an entertaining way, consistently — entertaining is the most important leg (Josh Braun — "Conversation with Kyle Crawford")
- **Jobs-To-Be-Done interview**: talk to 3-4 customers about life before/after buying and why the old way sucked; harvest their exact words as your messaging. Ask "Why this? Why now? Why not keep doing what you were doing?" — never "Why did you buy?" (Josh Braun — "Tough Love" / "Account Executive Coaching with Dave")
- Personalized-video sequence: LinkedIn connect w/ open loop → personalized research video walking a hypothesis → "Any thoughts?" email → voicemail + cold call (Josh Braun — "How to be a rockstar SDR - Charlotte Johnson")
- **"Breath point"**: stop asking questions and pivot to the recommendation at the natural lull in the conversation (Josh Braun — "How do defuse We're already working with a vendor")
- **CASSO** first-call framework: Confirm → Connect → frAme → Situation → Opportunities → Summarize (then Story/Value/Qualify/next step) (Josh Braun — "How to Lead an Initial Save Conversation")
- **References objection framework**: Pause → Defuse → Encourage → Golden Lasso → Respond. "Golden Lasso": "Let's say you speak with my clients and like what you hear — would you be ready to move forward today?" (Josh Braun — "How to defuse, I'd like to speak with some references")
- **Flower vs. Fireball**: features/specs are the flower (what you sell); the fireball is the awesome outcome the buyer gets — only sell fireballs (Josh Braun — "How to Lead an Initial Save Conversation")
- **Personal Trainer vs. Waiter**: a waiter takes orders, a trainer has a perspective and leads — be the trainer (Josh Braun — "How to Lead an Initial Save Conversation")
- 4 ways to make a prospect "more awesome": fix a pain, surface a hidden problem, tell them to do nothing (overkill), or point them elsewhere (Josh Braun — "How to Lead an Initial Save Conversation")
- JTBD zones: Green (progress, not a buyer) → Yellow → Orange → Red (high struggle = buyer); diagnose in 6-7 min, nurture the rest (Josh Braun — "How to Nurture Leads")
- "Top performers don't ask about problems, they find problems" — surface a hidden risk the prospect didn't know existed (Josh Braun — "How to Nurture Leads")
- **"What do you do" reframe**: never pitch the product — ask a question that lets the prospect self-identify the problem ("Ever put a wool sweater in the dryer and shrunk it?") before you answer (Josh Braun — "Zaza Takes the 'What do you do' Challenge")
- **"Magic statement" social-proof bridge**: "I hear this all the time — you remind me of another [role] who had the same issue; after working with us they [result]. Want to learn more?" (Josh Braun — "Zaza Takes the 'What do you do' Challenge")
- Use **"because"** to justify any ask — the printer-line study shows "because + reason" massively boosts compliance (Josh Braun — "How to defuse, I'd like to speak with some references")
- **Labeling > questions** (Chris Voss): convert a "why/what" question into a label — "It sounds like understanding how we tick is important to you" — to gather info without triggering defensiveness; mirror the last three words to keep someone talking (Josh Braun — "How to Rewire Your Brain to Listen - Chris Voss")
- **"Predictability builds trust"**: drop the word "trust"; instead tell them exactly when they'll hear from you and what happens next (Josh Braun — "How to Rewire Your Brain to Listen - Chris Voss")
- 3-part cold-call structure: (1) what to say at hello — reference a loose connection or create tension; (2) learn how they do the job today via a specific multiple-choice question that proves expertise; (3) illuminate a problem they don't know exists, flipping push → pull (Josh Braun — "Stop 'pitching' in a cold call")
- **Black-and-white infomercial test**: describe the prospect's BEFORE state so vividly (soggy fries, cut finger, hour cleanup) they see it — no product talk; specificity makes it visceral (Josh Braun — "Can You Pass the Infomercial Test")
- **"Problem prop, not value prop"**: open with the painful before-state, not your value proposition; the brain then auto-asks "what do you have for me?" What-you-do = the exact opposite of the before, in ONE sentence ("You've got acne — we help you get clear skin"). Use "so that you can…" to force the deeper benefit (Josh Braun — "Sales Messages That Motivates Prospects - Armand Farrokh")
- Every solution reduces to three outcomes: make money, save money, or prevent a lawsuit — never lead with "save time" (Josh Braun — "Sales Messages That Motivates Prospects - Armand Farrokh")
- **"Frequent + intense" problem test**: a problem only motivates a switch if it's both frequent and intense (one dead pixel vs. twenty) (Josh Braun — "Sales Therapy - Angela")
- **Desire scale 1–10**: don't pitch until the prospect is an 8–10; below ~5, drop them into nurture and reclaim your time (Josh Braun — "Account Executive Coaching with Dave")
- **Problem → Cause → Recommendation**: turn your POV into a free educational webinar/seminar on those three beats; lead with a deposit, not a pitch (Josh Braun — "Clarifying Your Message with Mohammed" / "Sales Therapy - Angela")
- **Detach from the "get"**: aim for truth (yes-interested or no-not-now), not the meeting — detaching makes you sound less salesy and close more (Josh Braun — "Stop 'pitching' in a cold call")

### VOC language
- "We're not interested at this time" / "I'm not interested" — true from their frame, because from their perspective the status quo is fine (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse, We're not interested")
- "I'd rather dance with the devil I know than change — change is very difficult. Nothing's a no-brainer, buddy." (switching-cost inertia) (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse, We're not interested")
- "I hate these passive-aggressive shaming emails. What a terrible practice. Fourth email and you haven't responded, so effing leave me alone." — real reply to a guilt-based break-up email (Josh Braun — "Ryan O'Hara Interview")
- Underlying causes behind "I don't want a 12-month contract": "Will this even work?", "Can I implement it given everything on my plate?", "If it doesn't work will I lose my job?" (Josh Braun — "Prospect says I don't want a 12-month contract")
- Real HR buyer (vs. marketing's "we streamline open enrollment"): "We were feeling really frazzled during open enrollment and we didn't want people banging on our door asking the same questions over and over about their benefits" (Josh Braun — "The 1 Mistake New Reps Make" / "Account Executive Coaching with Dave")
- "I don't even know what you're reaching out for" — the 8-9-in-10 response to vague, me-focused LinkedIn outreach (Josh Braun — "Darren Hull - Building Your Personal Brand")
- Generic me-too messaging to avoid (the "white circle"): "easy-to-use, sophisticated email marketing platform," "maximize revenue opportunities," "save HR professionals time and money," "account-based marketing end-to-end platform" (Josh Braun — "The One Thing..." / "Conversation with Kyle Crawford")
- Triathlete's own pain language: "around mile 57 my sit bones start to hurt, I get chafing, numbness, I have to get out of the saddle / out of the aero bars" (Josh Braun — "The One Thing Preventing You From Getting Higher Cold Email Response Rates")
- Vendor-incumbent phrasings to probe with "What do you mean by…": "we're pretty happy with them," "most of the reps are using it," "adoption is around 80%" (Josh Braun — "How do defuse We're already working with a vendor")
- "So what's in it for me?" — blunt brush-off to a free invite (Josh Braun — "Becc & Braun - Objection Chat")
- "I'd like to speak with some of your clients/references before I move forward" — often a polite smokescreen; real reasons hiding behind it: "I need a few weeks," "I need to talk to my boss," "be ready after our new VP joins," "our CFO needs to weigh in" (Josh Braun — "How to defuse, I'd like to speak with some references")
- "Buying something new is scary — is it gonna work? I already know the old thing. Am I gonna get fired if it doesn't work?" (Josh Braun — "Cold Calling - You're Doing it Wrong")
- "We get on meetings with people, they don't close, and our salespeople waste a lot of time following up and chasing — they're just not ready to buy right now." (Josh Braun — "Zaza Takes the 'What do you do' Challenge")
- "You sound like every other [salesperson] calling me that doesn't speak my language." (Josh Braun — "Cold Calling - You're Doing it Wrong")
- "Oh you caught me out of the blue / I'm so sorry, you did" — awkward-shock reaction to a cold opener (Josh Braun — "Inside Selling Podcast Morgan Gillespie")
- Pain stack salespeople fear: "I'm going to miss my numbers, I could miss my bonus, I may have to lay people off, I may lose my job." (Josh Braun — "How to Lead an Initial Save Conversation")
- Buyer's internal monologue on switching: "I've used this so long, I know the interface, I have a good rep relationship — even if yours is a little better it's not worth it; if I switch and it fails I could lose my job and reputation." (Josh Braun — "Sales Therapy - Angela")
- "The juice isn't worth the squeeze" — benefit perceived as smaller than the effort/money to switch (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse, Your Price is Too High")
- Real Weight Watchers buying language (vs. "I want to lose weight"): "I just got a divorce, my hair's falling out, I was fat, I wanted to meet a hot girl"; for women: "I didn't want my thighs to rub together when I put on a dress" (Josh Braun — "Account Executive Coaching with Dave")
- **"Commission breath"** — the visceral term for a rep who puts their interests before the buyer's (Josh Braun — "Stop 'pitching' in a cold call" / "Sales Therapy - Angela")
- LinkedIn testimonial framing built from customer words: "I don't kiss and tell, but my clients do" — harvested by asking "What was your life like before, and how is it better now?" (Josh Braun — "Alison Shutz on How to Land a Job Using LinkedIn")

### Offers / pricing / guarantees
- Risk-reversal that defuses "I don't want to commit before trying": "Would you be open to a 14-month contract where you could terminate without a penalty at any time in the first two months?" (Josh Braun — "Prospect says I don't want a 12-month contract")
- "Everybody deserves a plan" positioning: run the full analysis and hand over the plan regardless; value-first removes the "invoice for my time" friction (Josh Braun — "Darren Hull - Building Your Personal Brand")
- Qualify on price early to disqualify and shorten the cycle: "Generally speaking this requires an investment of between A and B — does that sound like it's in the realm of reality for you?" (Josh Braun — "kevin josh video")
- Sequence price AFTER value when the gain is unknown: diagnosis → "here's how we've helped companies like you" → then state the price, because "everything's too expensive if I don't know what I'll get for it" (Josh Braun — "kevin josh video")
- Free risk-reversal lead magnet driving opt-ins (the "Badass B2B Growth Guide") that itself converts some buyers (Josh Braun — "Behind the Scenes - How I Leverage LinkedIn to Generate Sales")
- Workshop/event offer: free dinner, not a lecture — "bring your email, we'll critique it; make a live cold call and maybe book a meeting on the spot" (Josh Braun — "How do defuse We're already working with a vendor")
- Free risk-reversal CTA: "Nothing can affect your revenue more than your sales conversations — for free, go to [URL]/talk, book time, and if it's a fit we'll talk about coaching." (Josh Braun — "How to Lead an Initial Save Conversation")
- Free diagnostic as offer wedge: "Would you like us to do a free leak test for you?" — a no-risk audit that surfaces a problem and moves the buyer to the red zone (Josh Braun — "How to Nurture Leads")
- Anchor price early and transactionally: "Based on what you're trying to achieve, [outcome] requires an investment of between 15 and 20K — we take Mastercard, Visa, Amex." Defuse with a "Do you have a Groupon?" joke (Josh Braun — "How to Lead an Initial Save Conversation")
- Opt-in nurture offer: "From time to time we send videos that teach you how to become a better [X] — would you be interested in getting those?" (Josh Braun — "How to Nurture Leads")
- Lead-magnet offer instead of a pitch: a free 1-on-1 virtual educational session — "We're doing online sessions for [role] on [outcome], showing the 3 things wrong with most [X]…" (Josh Braun — "Clarifying Your Message with Mohammed" / "Sales Therapy - Angela")
- Chet Holmes "buyers' pyramid": only ~3% are buying now but 100% will one day — offer education, not a demo, to the 97% (Josh Braun — "Clarifying Your Message with Mohammed")
- Price-anchor + practice offer: bundled book + course "Know Your Lines" at $49 — "it's a steal, I wish I had it when I was coming up" — anchored against memorizing your ~10–12 recurring objections (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse, Your Price is Too High")

### Objection handling
- Defuse "I'm not interested" instead of overcoming it: "That's not a problem — most people I speak with aren't interested when I call, I'm assuming that." Then isolate: "Is it that [outcome] isn't a priority, or is the timing bad?" (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse, We're not interested")
- **Mirror + Label** (Chris Voss): repeat "No yearly contract?" up-toned, or label "Seems like you don't want to commit before trying" — even a wrong label gets corrected; chase with "Sounds like there's more here than meets the eye" (Josh Braun — "Prospect says I don't want a 12-month contract")
- Discover the real blocker: "Contracts aside, what else are you up against?" (Josh Braun — "Prospect says I don't want a 12-month contract")
- Don't explain or talk people into things — "prospects can smell your commission breath." Understanding beats explaining (Josh Braun — "Prospect says I don't want a 12-month contract")
- Disarming cold-call openers: "You're probably gonna hate me — this is a cold call. Full transparency: want to hang up or roll the dice?" / "We've never spoken, but I was hoping you could help me out for a moment" (Josh Braun — "How to Nail the First 45 Seconds of a Cold Call")
- Disarming "take it or leave it" frame: "Not sure if this is something you'd be interested in, but…" — removes the assumption they need what you sell (Josh Braun — "Overcoming Call Reluctance with Tegan")
- Selling-as-service reframe for call reluctance: "If you had a heart attack and didn't know it, you'd be happy to take my call — so we'd be doing someone a disservice by not making them aware" (Josh Braun — "Overcoming Call Reluctance with Tegan")
- For unmotivated prospects, offer a low-friction nurture: "Looks like you're making adequate progress, but things change. Would it be okay if from time to time I sent you [useful content]?" (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse, We're not interested")
- "Just because you solve a problem doesn't mean they want to solve it right now" (grandma's toaster) — the win is staying top of mind for when they're in-market (Josh Braun — "The 1 Mistake New Reps Make")
- **"Red brick" pattern interrupt** for commodities: the copier rep who mails a brick-shaped sponge — be a memorable character so they remember how you made them feel, not what you sold (Josh Braun — "The 1 Mistake New Reps Make")
- Don't fight resistance — join it. To "your price is too high," pause two beats, mirror the last 2-3 words with an uptone, then "Seems like price is your only concern?" and shut up (Josh Braun — "4 Habits That Make Selling More Joyful")
- **"Walking the beach"**: if there's genuinely no problem, let them go — "Sounds like you've got this buttoned up… you're all taken care of, thanks for chatting" (shift from selling to sorting) (Josh Braun — "4 Habits That Make Selling More Joyful")
- "We already use a vendor" defuser: stay silent 2-3 seconds, then "Well, that's okay" (they expect a fight; calm it down). Reframe switching as adding, in the future: "Not for now, but at some point would you be open to seeing if there are opportunities beyond what you have today?" Seed doubt: "What outcome were you trying to achieve when you bought it? Why aren't the reps who aren't using it using it?" (Josh Braun — "How do defuse We're already working with a vendor")
- Self-deprecating disarm: "I wish I were a good enough salesperson to call right when the timing's perfect, but I'm not that good yet" (Josh Braun — "How do defuse We're already working with a vendor")
- "Send me information" brush-off: "Sure — just so I send something relevant, how do you do sales today?"; if they insist, name it: "Be honest — you're asking me to email because you don't plan to read it. Am I right?" then re-earn 2 minutes (Josh Braun — "kevin josh video")
- Don't justify your value — flip it: "I'm not sure this is a fit. What is it about [the offer] that piqued your interest?" then go quiet (Josh Braun — "Becc & Braun - Objection Chat")
- "Why should I select you?" → cleanse commission breath: "Wow, that's a great question — why WOULD you select me?" then "What would prompt you to switch from what you're using now to us?" (Josh Braun — "How to Rewire Your Brain to Listen - Chris Voss")
- Never overcome an objection — understand it; switching from "overcoming" to "understanding" makes it melt. Kill the word "why" (it triggers defensiveness); replace with "what"/"how" or a label (Josh Braun — "How to Rewire Your Brain to Listen - Chris Voss")
- Defusing statements memorized to slow the reflex to argue: "Of course my clients are better salespeople than I am," "That's not a problem," "I'd be happy to," "Sure thing, absolutely." (Josh Braun — "How to defuse, I'd like to speak with some references")
- "Only 5 minutes — can you give us a quick demo?" → "Happy to, but giving a demo before I understand your situation would do you a disservice — would it make sense to reschedule?" (Josh Braun — "How to Lead an Initial Save Conversation")
- "Why are you different?" → "Happy to tell you, but I don't want to assume why that matters to you — could I ask a few questions first?" (Josh Braun — "How to Lead an Initial Save Conversation")
- Angry cold-call moment ("How'd you get my number? You're calling at 6:30!") → disarm with humility + humor: "I'm so sorry, I thought I was calling the West Coast — I feel like such a jerk." (Josh Braun — "Why Cold Calling Gives You Anxiety")
- "I need to talk to my boss" → "That's okay — but let's say your boss said it was up to you, what would you say?" to test true buy-in (Josh Braun — "How to defuse, I'd like to speak with some references")
- Put the prospect in control to get the truth: use "would it make sense to…" instead of dictating next steps (the "don't touch the wet paint" effect). End by letting them lead: "Feels like we may be able to help — where would you like to go from here?" (Josh Braun — "How to defuse, I'd like to speak with some references" / "How to Lead an Initial Save Conversation")
- Diagnose first: is it an objection or a **"situational truth"** (real info like frozen budget / just made a hire)? Handle a truth like an objection and you kill rapport — "buyers are not liars" (Josh Braun — "How to Diffuse Objections With Matt Millen")
- Align + deflect, don't overcome: "I don't have budget." → "Of course you don't — I didn't ask you for any money. Nobody has money when I call the first time." Stay playful; "Do you have a Groupon?" (Josh Braun — "How to Diffuse Objections With Matt Millen")
- **Isolation question for price**: "Our price can be perceived as high at first. Let's put price aside — assuming it was in your budget, is this something you'd want to move forward with this week?" (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse, Your Price is Too High")
- "Your price is too high" has 5 possible causes: (1) no money and never will, (2) juice not worth the squeeze, (3) low motivation/no struggle, (4) no perceived difference vs. alternatives, (5) can't pay all at once (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse, Your Price is Too High")
- Situational-truth follow-up program: "Awesome you made a key hire — let me build an ROI on your numbers, no ask… it may cost you more NOT to do this." (Josh Braun — "How to Diffuse Objections With Matt Millen")
- Voss-style low-pressure CTA: "Would it be the worst idea to show you what this looks like on a call next week?" + accusation audit: "I know I'm calling at the worst time, I know you've got a bunch on your plate…" (Josh Braun — "Sales Messages That Motivates Prospects - Armand Farrokh")
- Take-away close on a discovery call: "If there's a fit we'll continue; if not, no problem — will you do me a favor and fire me after this call so I don't have to chase you with 50,000 follow-ups?" (Josh Braun — "Account Executive Coaching with Dave")
- **Reactance reframe**: "When prospects feel the push, they pull away" — peak curiosity and let them discover, so the prospect starts asking YOU questions (Josh Braun — "Stop 'pitching' in a cold call")

- "Greetings Chloe, I recently clocked your website using Google's mobile speed test and discovered you're likely losing lots of visitors due to load time on 4G..." — open with a personalized problem screenshot of THEIR site (Josh Braun — "Personalizing images at scale using Outreach")
- Photojojo shipping notice written FROM the product: "Dear Josh, Jelly Lens Kit here — I just found out I'm heading to you and couldn't be happier..." — humanize transactional touchpoints (Josh Braun — "Flip the Script")
- "Hi Nick, I got your name from a B2B list — congratulations on being list-worthy" — tension-breaker that calls out the cold reach honestly (Josh Braun — "Flip the Script")
- Crispy specific beats generic: "Josh, I know you're training for an Ironman, which means Saturday you're spending six hours on your bike — and at hour 3 you get numbness and have to get out of the aero bars because your lower back hurts" (Josh Braun — "Flip the Script")
- LinkedIn connect that gets ~6/10 accepts: "Here's a free 24-page guide to help [company] start more conversations with who they sell to. If you like it, let's connect. If not, send me your best objection. Either way, Godspeed." (Josh Braun — "Flip the Script")
- Curiosity-gap subject unrelated to the offer: "lost keys on Marshall Street" to market an entrepreneurship event — drove mass opens (Josh Braun — "Sarah Grosz - USC Talk")
- "Patrick, quick question" / "[Name], idea for [company]" subject lines pull 45–80% opens when paired with a personalized first line (Josh Braun — "Sales Therapy with Pat Downey")
- VOC-driven hook: woman said "every time I pick up the phone, I feel small" → straight into copy: "Do you feel small?" (Josh Braun — "Cold calling with Mohammed")
- Open on a true *situation* the whole segment shares, not a personalization: "Steve — end of the month and lots of commissions to pay." Personal, not personalized (Josh Braun — "How to Construct an Effective Cold Email")
- Crispy beats generic: not "we'll save you money on your sweater" but "Have you ever had a $325 cashmere sweater you accidentally put in the dryer and ruined?" (Josh Braun — "How to Increase Cold Email Response Rates with Patricia McLaren")
- Blame-flip hook: "When people aren't interested it's because you're not interesting" (Josh Braun — "Why Prospects Tell You They Aren't Interested")
- Red-X opener: "Every week I get 15 connection requests on LinkedIn and they are all the same and I ignore them" (Josh Braun — "Conversation with Rachel Gray")
- Counterintuitive hook: suggest the prospect NOT buy to surface real intent (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Push Your Prospects Away To Sell More Deals")
- Aspirational money hook with concrete before/after: "From 80k right out of college to 300K as an Enterprise AE in under five years" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "How Much Money Can You Make in Tech Sales?")
- Credential + curiosity-gap title formula: proof of scale + promised shortcut — "After Closing $250M in Deals, I Found a Faster Way to Sell" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "After Closing $250M in Deals")

### Frameworks / formulas
- The 4 silent yes-gates every prospect asks: 1) Should I pay attention to you? 2) Do I like you? 3) Can you help me solve a problem / do something better? 4) Are you credible? Fail one and you don't advance (Josh Braun — "Unleash 19" / "How to Increase Cold Email Response Rates with Patricia McLaren" / "Conversation with Rachel Gray")
- "Red X in a sea of white circles" — be the pattern-break; sounding like a stereotypical salesperson raises the anti-persuasion shield (Josh Braun — "Unleash 19" / "Cold Call Coaching with Cody" / "Cold Calling with Kendra Warlow")
- Four-rectangle calm cold-call frame: Open (ask permission) → Before (join the conversation in their head using VOC) → Illuminate (multiple-choice question on how they do the job today) → After (what gets better) (Josh Braun — "Cold calling that feels good on your soul")
- "Before & after": all sales/copy is what sucked before they paid vs. what got better after — mine LinkedIn comments for "before," testimonial pages for "after" (Josh Braun — "Cold calling that feels good on your soul")
- Struggle-ometer / Green Zone vs Red Zone (blue/yellow/orange/red): only red-zone prospects are buying; nurture green/yellow so you're top of mind when they hit red — don't push a demo on the unmotivated (Josh Braun — "Unleash 19" / "Flip the Script" / "How to Defuse 'I don't have a budget'")
- "Nine ways to give" for a strong first impression: answers, surprises, knowledge, experts, relevance, fame, props, clarity, flair — giving releases oxytocin (Josh Braun — "Unleash 19")
- "We help X with Y" positioning formula for LinkedIn headlines — lead with the problem you solve, not "I crush quota" (Josh Braun — "Unleash 19")
- Mad Libs email system: pre-write strong copy with 4 fill-in fields ("I came across your…", "really enjoyed…", an illumination question, end-on-a-high-note line) so reps personalize a whole sequence in 2 min not 15 (Josh Braun — "Sending personalized emails at scale")
- Peak-End rule: end emails on a high note (a "little adrenaline shot") so people remember and respond (Josh Braun — "Sending personalized emails at scale")
- 3x3 research: 3 facts in under 3 minutes per account; stop at the rabbit hole — finite reasons people buy = finite value props (Josh Braun — "Sara Colombo, Jellyvision")
- Multi-problem cold-call frame: "I don't know if this is a fit, but I was recently helping another [persona] struggling with A, B, and C — I don't suppose any of those resonate?" then shut up (Josh Braun — "Conversation With Sam")
- Objection loop: acknowledge/empathize → ask a question → double down on value (handle, don't rebut), rinse and repeat (Josh Braun — "Sara Colombo, Jellyvision")
- Defuser → Expand → Ask-for-the-sale sequence: memorized calming phrases, then questions to find the real struggle, then the if-then close (Josh Braun — "Defusing Objections with Jonah Silberg")
- Illumination / disruptive questions ("Are you aware…?", "Have you considered…?", "Have you ever had your gait checked?") create a problem by showing what's possible (Josh Braun — "Conversation With Sam" / "Flip the Script" / "Cold Calling with Kendra Warlow")
- "Closest to revenue" bucket priority: upsell customers → reactivate closed-lost → re-engage ghosted/inbound → intent/trigger → pure cold (last) (Josh Braun — "Sales Therapy with Sarah")
- Slow your tonality down more than feels natural so the brain registers "stranger / sales call" before you deliver value (Josh Braun — "Sara Colombo, Jellyvision")
- Sandwich method for prospecting videos: easy rapport open + prepared problem-centered middle + closing easy out; ask a question early so the brain "holds up its end" (Josh Braun — "Video Prospecting With Penelope Yamauchi")
- Purpose of a cold call is NOT to book a meeting — it's "to create an environment where the prospect feels comfortable telling you the truth" (yes/open or no/not now) (Josh Braun — "Do you hate cold calling")
- Red/yellow/green light: listen for confrontational energy and back off ("sounds like I came across the wrong way, my intent isn't to persuade you") instead of pushing (Josh Braun — "Do you hate cold calling" / "Cold Calling with Kendra Warlow")
- Deposits before withdrawals: make 3-4 educational "deposits" (free guide, map, mini-seminar — never a demo) before the ask; people reciprocate (Josh Braun — "Flip the Script")
- Sword vs. superpower: "People don't buy swords, they buy the superpower" — sell what the product lets them do, not the product (Josh Braun — "Flip the Script")
- "Floss one tooth" (BJ Fogg): shrink the scary action to the smallest first step — first cold call goal is just to find the right person (Josh Braun — "Do you hate cold calling")
- 4-line cold email: L1 = emotion/situation (true statement about their world, often humor); L2 = problem/stakes; L3 = third-party credibility; L4 = short low-friction CTA (Josh Braun — "How to Increase Cold Email Response Rates with Patricia McLaren")
- "Trigger → Teach → Third-party credibility → low-friction ask" structure; trigger = something observed about the prospect, 7 trigger types you can scale in a spreadsheet column (Josh Braun — "Sales Therapy with Pat Downey")
- 3-sentence cold email = Situation/Context line + "Think" line (a VOC question that reframes how they make progress) + Third-party validation ("X now does it in 5 min instead of 5 hrs") + soft CTA "worth a conversation?" (Josh Braun — "How to Construct an Effective Cold Email")
- Personalized vs. Personal: personalize = unique to one prospect; personal = a true situation the whole segment faces, so it scales — use personal as fallback (Josh Braun — "How to Construct an Effective Cold Email")
- Jobs-to-Be-Done / VOC mining: interview customers who bought in the last 30–45 days ("when did you first think this was a problem? what did you try before us? why happier now?") and lift exact lingo into a running Google Doc — never invent it (Josh Braun — "Sales Therapy with Pat Downey" / "Cold Call Coaching with Cody" / "Clarifying Your Sales Message with Jason")
- McDonald's milkshake JTBD: real buying reasons (one-handed long-commute breakfast) differ from marketing language (flavors/viscosity) — harvest buying language, not brand language (Josh Braun — "Sales Therapy with Pat Downey")
- Case-study mining: skip the marketing page, read "customer success stories" — the before/after challenges/solutions section is "the black-and-white version of the infomercial"; lift the quotes verbatim (Josh Braun — "How to Construct an Effective Cold Email")
- "Start with the familiar" to explain anything new: explain TiVo/Dropbox/Basecamp by contrasting against the old familiar way (VCR), not by naming the new category ("the cloud") (Josh Braun — "Jason Fried on the Art of Explanation")
- Features → Benefits via Mario: customer = Mario, product = the flower, the better thing they can now do = the fireball — "you're selling fireballs, not flowers" (Josh Braun — "Jason Fried on the Art of Explanation")
- "Bitching ain't switching": only repeated, frustrating struggle moments trigger change — stack real struggle quotes until the reader falls into the position (Josh Braun — "Jason Fried on the Art of Explanation")
- Problem-first not product-first: "We're Warmbox, can I get time on your calendar?" vs "51% of cold emails land in spam — how are you ensuring your SDRs' don't?" then shut up (Josh Braun — "What Is Progress In Sales?")
- Internal vs external problem: external = burnt grass / want green; internal/emotional = "I don't want the worst lawn on the street" — write to the deeper feeling (Josh Braun — "How to Increase Cold Email Response Rates with Patricia McLaren")
- Tactical-empathy 3-step for stalled deals: Label ("sounds like you're afraid that…") → silence → Mirror (last 3 words) → calibrated question ("how can we work together so you come out on top?") (Josh Braun — "Selling During a Pandemic with Becc & Braun")
- The Bucket Question: "I speak with [persona] all day. They all seem to struggle with [3 specific problems]. Does that sound like your world, or am I off base?" — establishes authority, makes it safe to admit; aim 70%+ yes (Kevin Dorsey via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "Use This Discovery Call Formula")
- Invert-the-benefit to find the problem: take your benefit (save time) → flip it (wasting time) → drill to the operational specific (manual data entry) (Kevin Dorsey via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "Use This Discovery Call Formula")
- Don't only sell on pain — also get the better future they desire: "What would this allow you to achieve? How would that feel?" then SELL the next step, not just set it (Kevin Dorsey via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "Use This Discovery Call Formula")
- VECS buyer-readiness model: Vetted / Educated / Cold / Self-service — meet the buyer where they are and compress the cycle instead of forcing every deal through 5 meetings (Jake Dunlap via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "Why Buyers Hate Your Sales Process")
- "Show up knowing nothing" pre-call email (48h before): "I talk to many [titles]. Some are already exploring options... others much earlier. Help me understand where you are so I can meet you prepared." (Jake Dunlap via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "Why Buyers Hate Your Sales Process")
- Greenfield "3 Whys": Why buy anything at all → Why buy you → Why buy you now (Jason Bay via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Outplay Competitors")
- TCO trap: don't sell "consolidate 5 tools, save $1k/mo" (starts a price war); sell what you UNLOCK (live inventory analysis saving $30–50k/project) (Jason Bay via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Outplay Competitors")
- Stage-based (not meeting-based) process — 5 agreements you GET, not meetings you DO: Problem → Priority → Evaluation → Value → Commercial (Mark via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "After Closing $250M in Deals")
- "321" qualification: 3 people, 2 departments, 1 decision-maker confirmed = real problem agreement (Mark via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "After Closing $250M in Deals")
- Problem ≠ want: a real problem is "an executive-level business initiative with a gap between current and needed performance" — that's what gets funded (Mark via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "After Closing $250M in Deals")

### VOC language
- "I've had great systems to keep my inbox manageable. I follow them for a week or two then gradually let it fill back to 15,000 emails, curse and hit delete all. It's a vicious cycle." (Josh Braun — "Cold calling that feels good on your soul")
- Mine testimonials for repeated emotional words — "calm" and "love" appeared 6+ times on the Hey email page; "love" is rare in software copy, worth swiping (Josh Braun — "Cold calling that feels good on your soul")
- PM VOC: "stuff is scattered in too many places," "there were gaps in our communication," "I felt like my hair was on fire," "I felt buried under email" (Josh Braun — "Helping Parker Fix His Sales Messaging" / "Clarifying Your Sales Message with Jason")
- HR/benefits VOC: "We want to be less frazzled during open enrollment. We want fewer people knocking on our doors asking the same questions until we pull our hair out." (Josh Braun — "Conversation With Sam")
- Dream-outcome reframe: not "photo tutorials" but "help parents take better pictures of their kids" (Josh Braun — "Helping Parker Fix His Sales Messaging")
- Anti-VOC jargon to avoid: "end-to-end scalable architecture," "strategic resources for strategic projects," "we're the Netflix of X," "cutting edge," "world-class," "award-winning," "the Uber of X," "disrupting/revolutionizing" (Josh Braun — "Unleash 19" / "Jason Fried on the Art of Explanation" / "How to Increase Cold Email Response Rates with Patricia McLaren")
- Emotional-word contrast: "the Wild West" (everyone goes off-brand) vs. "brand prison" (team checks everything all day instead of creating) (Josh Braun — "Cold Call Coaching with Cody")
- Buyer-language for an SDR's pain: "you make a hundred cold calls and barely talk to two or three people / send email after email and get little to no response" (Josh Braun — "Flip the Script")
- "Every time I pick up the phone, I feel small. The person I'm calling, I feel big… I reach for it but just when I'm about to pick it up, I reach away." (Josh Braun — "Cold calling with Mohammed")
- Captivate case-study pain language: "lots of manual data entry," "customizing reports for each rep," "hard-pasting Excel into Google Sheets," "running commissions in 5 minutes instead of 5 hours" (Josh Braun — "How to Construct an Effective Cold Email")
- Basecamp JTBD buying triggers: "we got more clients and couldn't keep track — things started falling through the cracks," "we got a high-profile client and wanted to be buttoned up," "couldn't hold people accountable" (Josh Braun — "Sales Therapy with Pat Downey")
- Triathlete pain lingo that signals you get them: "chafing," "numbness," "sit bones don't sit right," "around mile 37 I have to get out of the aero bars and the race takes longer" (Josh Braun — "Helping Morgan Level Up His Cold Call Skills" / "Why Prospects Tell You They Aren't Interested")
- Dig past the stated reason: nightlight buyer's surface reason "to read in bed" masked the real outcome "to save my marriage" (read without waking his wife) (Josh Braun — "How to Increase Cold Email Response Rates with Patricia McLaren")
- Buyer reaction to templated outreach: "love your podcast, here's my pitch" — the disjointed flattery-then-pitch pattern buyers hate; "stench of sales and marketing line" (Josh Braun — "Conversation with Rachel Gray" / "Why Prospects Tell You They Aren't Interested")
- Buyer "self-service" voice: "I already know the space, I've bought this 3x, I care about your success team — sorry seller, love you, but can I just talk to those people?" (Jake Dunlap via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "Why Buyers Hate Your Sales Process")
- 30K purchase psychology: "Nobody wakes up wanting to spend 30K... they couldn't take it anymore, a bunch of things happened before they fired the old thing," plus the fear "Will it work? Am I gonna get fired?" (Josh Braun — "Why Prospects Tell You They Aren't Interested")
- Controller's day: "chasing down receipts, buried at month-end closing the books, transactions don't match" (Kevin Dorsey via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "Use This Discovery Call Formula")

### Offers / pricing / guarantees
- Three-tier offer ladder: $197 self-serve resource guide (one-time, lifetime updates) → $497 14-day cohort challenge with feedback → $1,600 four 1-on-1 coaching sessions; recommend by diagnosed need, not price (Josh Braun — "Sales Therapy with Sarah")
- Risk-reversal micro-offer: "Send me a cold email and I'll send you a revision — no cost, no ask. If you like it, let's talk." (Josh Braun — "Sending personalized emails at scale")
- "Cost-neutral" reframe: position the apprentice-to-hire model so the buyer's existing spend (6–8K/mo OTE + benefits) covers it, neutralizing the recruiter-fee objection; fixed annual subscription for 2+ hires = unlimited hiring (Josh Braun — "Video Prospecting With Penelope Yamauchi")
- Never discount — add value instead (throw in a feature/module for the first 6 months) to protect price and avoid setting a discounting precedent (Josh Braun — "Defusing Objections with Jonah Silberg")
- Reframe the cold-call ask as a no-agenda offer of value: "I don't even know if what we have is a fit, I'm just calling to see if you'd be open to some new ideas" (Josh Braun — "Sales Therapy with Pat Downey")
- Discovery opener that flips the floor to the prospect: "I could tell you a million things about us… but first I'd love to hear about you." ~85% then talk uninterrupted for minutes (Josh Braun — "Sam & Josh Chat Sales")
- "Sell the meeting, not the product": first email uses emotion to sell the time/call; sell the rest in the hour — don't blast features up front (Josh Braun — "How to Increase Cold Email Response Rates with Patricia McLaren")
- Pre-price validation sequence before revealing the number: confirm (1) value agreement independent of price, (2) process agreement (who approves, how long), (3) pricing-structure alignment — then state the number and go silent (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Learn How to Negotiate High Ticket Deals")
- Price-reveal mechanic: explain how pricing works BEFORE the number, give the number, then shut up — "whoever speaks first loses" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Learn How to Negotiate High Ticket Deals")
- Trade-off negotiation: never give a concession for free — "every time they ask for something, I ask for something in return"; tenderize with a long fight so the final concession feels like they "won the lottery" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Learn How to Negotiate High Ticket Deals")
- Anchor-honesty close: "We're never the cheapest, but never totally out of the realm — what did you have in mind? Do you have a real number or just asking for a discount?" (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Learn How to Negotiate High Ticket Deals")
- Manufactured-scarcity approval email: CC the CEO, send 4 hours later (looks like you fought for approval), agreed terms in big red letters + deadline + what happens if it slips (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Learn How to Negotiate High Ticket Deals")

### Objection handling
- "Why are you different/better than [competitor]?" → "I'm not sure we are — I don't want to assume why I think we're different matters to you. Would it be okay if I asked a few questions first to see if we're even a fit?" (Josh Braun — "Defusing Objections with Jonah Silberg")
- Isolate the real objection with the if-then "moment of truth": "Price aside — assume price is out of the equation — is there anything else stopping you from moving forward this week?" (Josh Braun — "Defusing Objections with Jonah Silberg")
- On price say "have price aside" not "let's talk through price" (which signals wiggle room/discount); if it's purely lowest-price, bow out gracefully — "we'd be doing you a disservice" (Josh Braun — "Defusing Objections with Jonah Silberg")
- "Send me information" → "I have more info than anyone needs — let me ask a couple questions so I send the most relevant stuff." Can't articulate = smokescreen; leans in = interest (Josh Braun — "Sara Colombo, Jellyvision" / "Cold calling with Mohammed")
- When prospect already has a vendor/coach: don't judge or pitch — understand. "Sounds like you've got this covered," let them feel heard, then move to a problem they may not see (Josh Braun — "Cold Call Critique")
- Core fix for a stalled call: "Move off the solution, into the problem. Your solution has no value without a problem." Ask "are you working with someone already?" from the jump (Josh Braun — "Cold Call Critique")
- Accusation audit (Voss): proactively label the negative — "I know my timing is terrible" — labeling negatives diffuses them (Josh Braun — "Cold calling that feels good on your soul" / "Selling During a Pandemic with Becc & Braun")
- Release attachment to the outcome — prospects "smell your commission breath" when you push; aim only to surface the truth (yes-open / no-not-now), which melts call anxiety (Josh Braun — "Cold calling that feels good on your soul" / "What Is Progress In Sales?")
- Give an easy out to lower resistance: "If you can't, no problem at all" signals no pressure and hands the prospect control/autonomy → more truth (Josh Braun — "Video Prospecting With Penelope Yamauchi" / "The Smoothest Cold Call Ever With Heidi Briones")
- Mirror, don't overcome: "I don't have any failed payments" → "No failed payments?" + "That's no problem" + pass-the-potato question "how do you KNOW you don't have failed payments?" (Josh Braun — "Cold Calling with Kendra Warlow")
- Truth vs. smokescreen: use "Golden Lasso" questions before responding — "Budget aside, is this even a tool you like?" then "Where does this sit on your list — a 1, a 5, a 10?" (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse 'I don't have a budget'")
- Don't treat a truth like an objection (a real frozen budget / just-made-a-hire) — handle it and you kill rapport; "buyers are not liars" (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse 'I don't have a budget'" / "How to Diffuse Objections With Matt Millen")
- "Let me talk to my boss" → "Say it were up to you — would you move forward? When you take it to her, what objection will she raise and how will you handle it?" (Josh Braun — "How to Defuse 'I don't have a budget'")
- Red-light recovery via self-deprecation: "I'm so sorry, I thought I was calling the west coast — I feel like such a jerk." Nothing diffuses sales pressure like self-deprecating humor (Josh Braun — "Do you hate cold calling")
- Negatively-framed problem-finder (takeaway): "I'm assuming you guys don't have that problem — you're good that way?" — safer than "Do you have this problem?" (Josh Braun — "Cold Call Coaching with Cody" / "Helping Morgan Level Up His Cold Call Skills")
- Low-friction "No is safe" CTAs (Voss): "Are you open to a lesser-known idea that might help…?" / "Would it be a terrible idea if we had a quick email exchange to see if a conversation even makes sense?" close with "Either way, keep up the great work" (Josh Braun — "Flip the Script")
- "Nothing was wrong with my Breville until I saw the Vitamix make hot soup" — disarm the no-pain prospect by showing what's possible; a problem isn't a problem until you name it (Josh Braun — "Sales Therapy with Pat Downey")
- Detach to avoid the "zone of resistance": pushing triggers fight-or-flight; use a "metal detector" — only dig when you get a beep (a real problem signal) (Josh Braun — "What Is Progress In Sales?")
- "Push away to get truth" — suggest a non-you alternative ("Have you considered just hiring another AR clerk?"); their defense reaffirms your value or surfaces the real objection (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Push Your Prospects Away To Sell More Deals")
- Pressure-test the price objection: "You said this is twice what you pay now — that's a big jump, how are you feeling?" surfaces real budget block vs. negotiation tactic (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Push Your Prospects Away To Sell More Deals")
- Name the deal-killer: "Emma seemed skeptical — does she have a point?" — either answer gets you to truth (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Push Your Prospects Away To Sell More Deals")
- "Chunk up" the feature-gap objection: competitor "has X and you don't" → "before we dig in, what are you trying to accomplish through that?" then show another way to solve it (Jason Bay via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Outplay Competitors")
- Address competitors head-on: "I imagine you're looking into other vendors — who else, and what are you looking for?" — position your differentiators early, not mid-cycle (Jason Bay via 30 Minutes to President's Club — "How to Outplay Competitors")
- Distinguish "the BS 'I want it cheaper'" from a real anchor ("your three competitors cost X") — only the real answer is workable (30 Minutes to President's Club — "Learn How to Negotiate High Ticket Deals")
